strengths: CUDA kernel optimization with real memory-hierarchy work - VGG16 project: replaced TorchScript conv layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights/biases, preallocated global buffers; 49.2ms coalesced vs 73.3ms uncoalesced (~35% speedup), 1.5-2x on convolutions
GPU memory profiling and quantization - TinyLlama 1.1B 8-bit (LLM.int8) cut VRAM ~55% with <1% accuracy loss, profiled peak VRAM/latency with pynvml
LLM internals + accelerator deployment - GPT-2 built from scratch (multi-head attention, MLP, layer norm, weight tying); TensorRT-optimized YOLO on Jetson at 5.2x speedup (56.7 -> 10.9ms)

Parallel performance reasoning at scale - MPI ray tracer, 4 work-distribution strategies, 30x speedup; Hodgkin-Huxley 10.49x with load-imbalance characterization (65% degradation under uneven distribution)
Coursework backs it: High Performance Architecture, Multiple Processor Systems
real_gaps: Compiler stack is entirely absent - JD names OpenXLA, MLIR, Triton, code generation, runtime systems, and lists 'ML compiler cost model design' as a core responsibility. No IR-level or compiler-development work anywhere in the profile.
Triton and CUTLASS are named in the MINIMUM quals, not preferred. Hand-written CUDA C++ is the same family but not the same toolchain.

CUDA depth stops below the level this role lives at - no shared-memory tiling, bank conflicts, tensor cores/WMMA, warp-level primitives, occupancy tuning, or double buffering evident. Coalescing + constant memory is the entry tier.
Profiling tooling gap - pynvml is a coarse device-query API, not a kernel profiler. No Nsight Compute, nvprof, or CUPTI. GPU performance work is roofline and warp-stall analysis.
Scale mismatch - all GPU work is single-GPU, single-author academic/personal projects. JD is fleet-scale, cross-node model serving, billions of users. No multi-GPU, NCCL, or distributed inference.
GPU-specific experience is project-scoped, not employment-scoped - none of the 7 internships were GPU performance roles (they were ML research, CV, embedded).
overstated_by_keywords: 'Kernel optimization' and 'memory coalescing' as skill-list entries - both trace to one course project, at the introductory optimization tier
Triton / CUTLASS counted Adjacent via CUDA C++ - genuinely weaker; each has its own idioms and the JD names them explicitly
'AI accelerators' via Jetson - Jetson is edge inference; the JD means datacenter GPUs (A100/H100-class). Different performance regime.
TensorRT/ONNX/TorchScript counted toward 'compiler optimization and runtime systems' - these are consumed as black boxes, not developed
'Memory hierarchies' - one technique (global-memory coalescing), not shared memory / L2 / register-file reasoning
llm_analysis.reasoning: The core minimum qual (low-level GPU programming plus performance engineering) is genuinely met, with a real CUDA project carrying honest before/after numbers, and the LLM preferred qual is a real strength. But the keyword score of 100% is inflated: it credits CUDA C++ for Triton and CUTLASS, Jetson for datacenter accelerators, and TensorRT for compiler work. The two responsibilities Google weights most (ML compiler cost model design, cross-node serving) have no backing in the profile at all. This is a legitimate application that clears the bar on paper, but it will compete against candidates with production Triton/CUTLASS and MLIR experience.
